grammar.label: past perfect — form and use
grammar.meaning: an event finished before another past event

explanation.en: Use had + past participle for the earlier of two past events. The later event stays in the past simple.
explanation.uz: Ikki o'tgan voqeadan avvalgisi uchun had + III shakl ishlatiladi. Keyingi voqea past simple da qoladi.

grammar.positive_example: When I arrived, the train had already left.
grammar.negative_example: When I arrived, the train already left.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada tartib ko'pincha 'oldin/keyin' so'zlari bilan beriladi, alohida zamon bilan emas.

grammar.label: past perfect vs past simple in narrative
grammar.meaning: background against foreground in a story

explanation.en: In a story the past simple carries the main line of events. The past perfect steps back to explain what had happened before.
explanation.uz: Hikoyada asosiy voqealar past simple bilan beriladi. Past perfect esa undan oldin nima bo'lganini tushuntirish uchun orqaga qaytadi.

grammar.positive_example: She was tired because she had worked all night.
grammar.negative_example: She was tired because she has worked all night.

l1_notes.uz: Past perfect faqat boshqa o'tgan voqeaga nisbatan ishlatiladi, yolg'iz o'zi emas.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: You missed an incident at the station last night.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: By the time I arrived, a crowd had already gathered.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: A small fire in a shop. Fortunately nobody was injured.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Had it started before the shop closed?

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Yes. The owner had left an hour before, so the shop was closed.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: Very. A bystander had noticed the smoke and called for help.

body.speaker: Bobur
body.text: It had not worked for months. Somebody had reported it, but nothing was done.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is what worries me, not the fire.
